chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from al-Husayn ibn Muhammad from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad from al-Hasan ibn Ali from Hammad ibn 'Uthman said:

I said to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), 'What is the ta'zir (disciplinary punishment)?' He said, 'Less than the hadd (fixed punishment).' I said, 'Less than eighty?' He said, 'No, but it is less than forty, for that is the hadd of the slave.' I said, 'And how much is that?' He said, 'Ali (peace be upon him) said: According to what the ruler sees of the man's sin and the strength of his body. So the way to understand this report is to carry it on taqiyyah (dissimulation), for it is the view of some of the Sunnis.'
ai.seo_question: What is the difference between hadd and ta'zir punishments for drinking in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith clarifies the distinction between the fixed hadd of forty lashes for a slave and the discretionary ta'zir for intoxication, which varies according to the ruler's assessment of the offender's capacity and the severity of the sin. The narration attributes this flexibility to taqiyyah, reflecting the Imam's strategic alignment with prevailing Sunni legal opinions to avoid confusion or political friction. This highlights the dynamic nature of judicial discretion in Shia jurisprudence, where the wali al-amr plays a central role in determining appropriate disciplinary measures.
